# javaabu/settings

> Settings for Laravel, defined once with javaabu/stencil: a setting's key, default, input and validation in one place (Setting::make('per_page')->default(20)->integer()). Settings are grouped into pages and sections; Route::settings() gives each page a form, validation, saving and a page in Blade (javaabu/forms) or Inertia React (@javaabu/forms, shipped through javaabu/manifest). Values are typed, cached, and reloaded by queue workers and Octane when they change. A policy and permissions come from javaabu/permissions; translatable settings from javaabu/translatable; an activity log from spatie/laravel-activitylog.

Paths are relative to this file. In a project, that's vendor/javaabu/settings/.

## Rules

- Define every setting with `Javaabu\Settings\Definitions\Setting::make('key')`, on a `SettingsPage` class (`definition()`), an inline page (`Settings::page('mail')->schema(fn () => [...])`) or with `Settings::define([...])` for settings without a page. Don't add new keys to `config/defaults.php`; that's the v1 fallback.
- Put the default, the field and the validation on the setting: `->default(20)->field(TextInput::class)->integer()->minValue(1)->required()`. Methods the setting doesn't have go to the stencil field. Never validate settings in a controller.
- Read with `settings('key')` (or `Settings::get()`, or v1's `get_setting()`); use the typed getters (`settings()->integer('per_page')`, `string()`, `boolean()`, `float()`, `array()`) where the type matters. Don't cast by hand: values come back as the field's type, enums with `->cast(Enum::class)`.
- Write with `Settings::set([...])` (saved straight away, no `save()`). Don't write to the `settings` table or the cache directly: writes bump the version that workers check.
- Register the settings routes yourself with `Route::settings([...])` in the app's route group; pass `guard`, `prefix` and `name` for an admin portal. They aren't loaded automatically. Add `Route::stencil()` once if a setting uses `->live()`.
- Permissions are `view_settings` and `edit_settings`, plus each page's own `$permission`. Run `php artisan permissions:sync`. Override the policy with `config('permissions.policies')` or `Gate::policy(SettingsPage::class, ...)`.
- Secrets: `->encrypted()`. They're never sent to the browser; an empty input keeps the value. Don't add `required()` to them.
- Files: `->field(ImageUpload::class)` stores a path on `config('settings.disk')`; show it with `settings()->url('logo')`.
- Use a cache store every process shares (Redis, database, file) when running queue workers or Octane; never tell users to restart workers after changing settings.
- Labels, help texts, page labels and options go through `__()`. Add `->thaana()` to text settings that take Dhivehi; `->translatable()` for a value per language.
- In tests, use `Settings::fake([...])` or the `FakesSettings` trait (`setFakeSetting()`); don't mock the facade.
